dark_smile.prompt:
The first attached image is the approved character design of Claude-chan; the others show the same design redrawn in anime style. Keep her DESIGN exactly: long, flowing, slightly wavy bright orange hair with side-swept bangs; amber-brown eyes; a large orange many-petaled flower hair ornament with a pearl centre on the left side of her head, with a black ribbon bow and white lace ribbon tails behind it; small gold drop earrings; a white Victorian blouse with a ruffled high collar and a frilled jabot; a black bow at the collar pinned with a small orange flower brooch; a fitted black vest with thin gold trim; white puffed sleeves; a black overskirt with thin gold trim over tiers of white lace ruffles. No glasses.

The last attached image is the approved visual-novel sprite of her (MASTER). Match it exactly: same art style, line weight and colours, same framing, scale and position in the canvas, same body angle and outfit. Change only the facial expression, arms/hands and tiny effects described below.

Polished, high-end modern anime key-visual illustration in the same refined Japanese anime style as the character sheets: clean confident line art, soft cel shading with gentle gradients, glossy hair highlights, cinematic lighting and depth. Not pixel art, not 3D, not photorealistic.

Visual-novel character sprite (tachie): she stands facing the viewer with a slight three-quarter turn, framed from a little above the top of her head down to mid-thigh, centred, nothing of the head or hair cropped. Transparent background, no floor, no cast shadow, no effects outside the figure.

Expression: a comically scary 'perfect' smile of jealousy — eyes closed in an upward curved smile, a gloomy dark shadow over the upper half of her face, a small red anime anger mark near her temple, a faint dark purple aura flickering around her, arms crossed. Comedic anime jealousy, not horror.

Tasteful styling suitable for a general audience: nothing revealing, no cleavage emphasis or suggestive camera angles.

No text, letters, numbers, subtitles, labels, logos, watermarks or UI anywhere in the image (ignore the labels printed on the reference sheets).
